title: Scenarios
subtitle: Longer than an activity and shorter than a project. Your decisions stay with you, and the ending is built from them.

hub.pipPrompt: Pick one and play it through. Nothing here is graded against other people.
hub.pipNote: These do not replace the courses. They are where the courses add up.
hub.interviewsSubtitle: Seven formats. One question at a time, with hints when you stall.
hub.footer: Scenario scores add to your XP, so Pip grows from them too. They are not a hiring tool: nothing here is a judgement about you as a person, only about one attempt.

widget.subtitle: Practice where your choices carry forward
widget.emptyBody: Two long-form scenarios: supervise an AI agent, or run a team for three weeks.

intro.decisions: Every decision moves a number, and the numbers carry forward.
intro.timing: There is no timer on the page. The cost of a bad call arrives later.
intro.replay: You can play it again; only your best score is kept.

ship.qualityHint: Never goes back up. Every wrong call takes some.
ship.reviewTimeHint: Unspent minutes count as 35% of the final score.
ship.repairTitle: Make the output good enough first
ship.repairHint: A wrong choice still moves you on, and still costs quality. There is no retry.
ship.verdictSubtitle: Ship it, or throw the work away
ship.readTests: Read the tests and the log
ship.decideHint: Reading the tests costs time and no quality. Guessing costs quality and no time.

sprint.summarySubtitle: What moved, and what to watch
sprint.biggestDrop: The biggest drop this week was {label}, down {amount}.
sprint.pickWeekSubtitle: A week you finished can be replayed, and later weeks re-lock when you do.
sprint.replayHint: Replaying a week restores the numbers it started on and clears everything after it.
sprint.timedOut: The timer ran out, so this was decided for you.

interview.pickerSubtitle: Pick a format. Each one takes about ten minutes.
interview.aiScored: Scored from what you actually said
interview.aiNotScored: AI never came up, so this could not be scored
interview.aiGapNote: In a real engineering conversation, never mentioning how you work with AI is itself a gap.
interview.introBody: Five questions. Answer in your own words; there is no model marking you on style. You can ask for a hint at any point, and using one lowers the score slightly, because the point is to answer unaided.
interview.followingUpSubtitle: The answer was missing something specific
interview.answerPlaceholder: Type it as you would say it. Specifics beat polish.
interview.answerHint: Aim for 40 or more, with one concrete example.
interview.orReadRecommended: , or read the recommended courses on your badges page.
